The quality of life of women with breast cancer is affected in the long term.
breast-conserving therapy (BCT) in Thailand results in good cosmetic outcome, high patient satisfaction, and good health-related quality of life (QOL) for women with breast cancer.

the use of the MDT in the management of breast cancer in Thailand has resulted in a reduction of the local recurrence rate, a decrease in the use of mastectomy and a significant improvement in cosmetic outcome and quality of life in women treated with breast conserving therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of life of women who have been treated for breast cancer.
the quality of life of breast cancer patients after breast conserving therapy.
the effects of breast-conserving treatment for breast cancer on quality of life and cosmetic outcomes in a group of Thai women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
breast conserving therapy is as good as mastectomy in terms of survival, but it is associated with a better cosmetic outcome and a better quality of life.

the quality of life of breast cancer survivors who undergo breast conserving therapy is similar to that of breast cancer survivors undergoing mastectomy, and both groups of women have a better quality of life than healthy women.

the quality of life of Thai women post breast-conserving therapy for breast cancer is not affected in terms of the cosmetic outcomes, but it is affected in terms of physical, social and emotional domains.

the quality-of-life impact of breast-conserving therapy for early-stage breast cancer is similar to the quality-of-life effect of mastectomy.
